subscriptions/notify.after_answers.cite:
activesupport-7.1.6 lib/active_support/log_subscriber.rb, which gains a whole mechanism in this release: :88 `class_attribute :log_levels`, :90-94 `LEVEL_CHECKS = { debug: ->(logger) { !logger.debug? }, info: ..., error: ... }`, :131-134 `subscribe_log_level(method, level)`, :146-148 `silenced?(event) = logger.nil? || @event_levels[event]&.call(logger)`, and :162 `attr_writer :event_levels`.  activesupport-7.0.10's copy of that file contains neither `subscribe_log_level` nor `silenced?` (grep count 0 for both).  The plumbing that consults it is also new: activesupport-7.1.6 lib/active_support/notifications/fanout.rb:385 `@silenceable = delegate.respond_to?(:silenced?)`, :408-409 `silenced?(name) = @silenceable && @delegate.silenced?(name)` and :311 `all_listeners_for(name).reject { |s| s.silenced?(name) }` -- activesupport-7.0.10's fanout.rb has no occurrence of the word at all.
The two declarations that retune these particular lines: actionmailer-7.1.6 lib/action_mailer/log_subscriber.rb:25 `subscribe_log_level :deliver, :debug` (the method it applies to is :10-24, whose body still calls `info`), and actionview-7.1.6 lib/action_view/log_subscriber.rb:24 `subscribe_log_level :render_template, :debug` (method at :14-23, body still calls `info`).  Neither line exists in the 7.0.10 copies of those two files.  Note :43 in the same 7.1.6 file, `subscribe_log_level :render_layout, :info` -- the release moved these four Action View events individually, and kept the layout line where it was.
The level this application runs at: config/environments/production.rb:59, `config.log_level = :info`, unchanged by this step and unchanged since the 4.2 baseline.  `logger.debug?` is therefore false, `silenced?` is therefore true, and the fanout drops both subscribers before the event is published.
Measured: /tmp/step08-oracle/logs/verifier/observed.json, world `subscriptions` -- `.stdout` len=2 on the step 07 golden, len=0 on the step 08 golden, with `exit_ok`, `aborted`, `exception` and `task` byte-identical.  Measured the other way as well, on the same trees under RAILS_ENV=production: build/probe08/log2.rb writes `Rails.logger.info` and `ActionMailer::Base.logger.info` directly and both lines appear (build/probe08/out/log2-*.json records the logger as an `ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger` at level 1 over an `ActiveSupport::Logger`, with `ActionMailer::LogSubscriber` and `ActionView::LogSubscriber` both attached), so the logger is alive, the subscribers are attached, and what changed is the level the two events are published at.
subscriptions/notify.after_answers.why:
Rails 7.1 moved `Delivered mail ...` and `  Rendered <template>` from info to debug, and this application logs at info in production, so the two lines this case recorded are no longer written.  They are the whole of the case's `.stdout`, so it goes from two entries to none.
Nothing else about the case moves: `exit_ok` is still true, `aborted` still false, `exception` still null, and the rake task is still `notifications:send`.  Nor is this the mail going missing -- the companion `*_mail` case at the same scenario point records the delivered message (envelope, subject, headings) and is unchanged at this rung, which is what separates `the line is no longer logged` from `the mail is no longer sent`.  spec/mailers/notification_mailer_spec.rb asserts the delivery independently and still passes, 504 examples 0 failures.
Not worked around.  The only lever the release leaves is `config.log_level = :debug` in production, which would restore these two lines by also restoring every SQL statement, every partial render and every cache read -- a far larger change to the recorded worlds, made to preserve a log line the framework deliberately demoted.  Rails 7.1 reclassified them as diagnostics; this ladder takes the release's default, records the new answer, and cites it.
  This is the first of the three: the digest that goes out after the opinion and message scenario steps have run.
